## 1. `wiki/CONVENTIONS.md` (the schema layer; read before any ingest)

**Node types** — one-level directories map 1:1 to **eight ontology node types**, plus a ninth non-ontology namespace:

| Namespace | Notes |
|---|---|
| `framework/` | SDLC agent toolkit/methodology. Edge `runs_on:` → harness |
| `capability/` | One unit of work a framework exposes. `subtype: command \| skill \| sub-agent` |
| `sdlc-stage/` | **Derived projection** from `implements:` backlinks; framework-neutral naming; re-derived every ingest |
| `artifact/` | Concrete output a capability produces |
| `pattern/` | Reusable technique; **the seam** where runtime *and* harness attach via `enables:` |
| `harness/` | The agent program/loop. `subtype: terminal \| ide`. The pivot the other layers are defined against |
| `runtime/` | Agent execution/orchestration substrate. `subtype: library \| platform`. Edges: `runs:` → harness, `enables:` → pattern. **No** `implements:`/`belongs_to:`/`equivalent_to:` |
| `store/` | Durable agent-facing state. `subtype: work \| memory`. `integrates_with:` → harness |
| `topic/` | **Explicitly NOT an ontology node** — curated navigation overlay above the graph |

Four-layer framing in the preamble: framework/harness/runtime are all *compute* (instructions, the loop, where the loop runs — transient per run); store is *state* (survives the run).

**§"The execution layer (runtimes)" (line ~248)** is directly relevant to your restructuring:
- Explicit note that `runtime` is an **overloaded word** (language/container/model runtime); the *layer* is called "the execution layer", the *node* is `runtime`; "where the two names sit side by side, the layer name is the one that carries the meaning."
- Explicit rejection of renaming the node to **`orchestrator`**, with four reasons: orchestration is only 3 of 9 synthesized dimensions (isolation and persistence aren't orchestration); a `library`-subtype runtime is a toolkit you *script* orchestration with; orchestration also happens at the process layer (`pattern-wave-parallelism`) and in the harness (sub-agent spawning); naming the node for it "would imply a monopoly the evidence does not support."
- **Ingest recipe for a runtime:** source → `raw/runtime/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md`; create `wiki/runtime/<name>.md` with `type: runtime` + `subtype:` + `enables:`; stub any new pattern pages; add an **"Enabled by (infrastructure)"** subsection to each enabled pattern; refresh the `## runtime` matrix in `catalogue.md`; log it. No stage re-derivation.
- **Anti-premature-abstraction rule** (repeated for runtime, harness, and store): synthesis dimensions live as a **comparison matrix in the layer's `index.md`** and as prose per page — *not* minted as their own derived-node namespace. "Graduate the matrix into derived nodes only if the layer grows enough that it stops scaling."

**Naming convention (§line 198)** — designed to guarantee globally unique basenames (wikilinks resolve by basename, Obsidian/Tolaria style): framework `<framework>`; capability `<framework>-<name>`; sdlc-stage `stage-<name>`; artifact `artifact-<name>`; pattern `pattern-<name>`; harness `<harness>`; **runtime `<runtime>`** (bare, e.g. `sandcastle`, `warren`); store `<store>`; topic `topic-<name>`. Files at `wiki/<namespace>/<basename>.md`, kebab-case, ≤60 chars. Renaming is described as "a cascade — do it safely and atomically" (§line 345).

**Index pages / aggregation rules (§"The topic layer", line 284)** — a table of **four distinct aggregation mechanisms** that "must not be confused":
- `catalogue.md` — exhaustive, one section per namespace, **mechanical**; `index.md` is "the authored introduction that points into it"
- `sdlc-stage` — bottom-up, **derived** from backlinks
- `pattern` — bottom-up, from `apply:` edges
- `topic` — **top-down**, hand-picked cross-namespace links, open-ended, may be opinionated

Topic overlay rules: no stored ontology edges; a topic link is **never evidence**; do not hand-author "Referenced by topic X" rosters. Discipline gate: a topic earns a page only when the theme spans **≥3 namespaces** *and* a reader couldn't assemble it from an existing page; "When a topic's whole content could live as a section on one existing page, put it there instead."

**Formatting (§line 356):** enumerate capabilities as bullet lists, one per line, `[[wikilink]] — short role note`; group long rosters under bold sub-headings; tables only for fixed multi-column data.

**No glossary convention exists** in CONVENTIONS.md.

## Part 1 — awesome-loop-engineering

**Source:** https://github.com/ChaoYue0307/awesome-loop-engineering (the github.io page is a front for it; dataset mirror at huggingface.co/datasets/cy0307/awesome-loop-engineering)

**Definition.** "Loop engineering" = designing recurring systems that discover work, delegate it to agents, verify results, persist state, decide next actions, and run again on a cadence, event, or until a verifiable goal is reached. Explicitly positioned as the layer *above* prompt/context/harness engineering: harness engineering surrounds one run; loop engineering decides when and why the run happens again.

**Taxonomy.** The repo has both a section structure and a formal TAXONOMY.md:
- Sections: Loop Contract (11 decision parts: objective, trigger, discover/intake, workspace, context, delegation, verification, state, budget, escalation, exit) · Lifecycle (Intake → Delegate → Act → Verify → Persist → Decide) · Pattern Library (22 playbooks, e.g. PR Babysitter, CI Repair Loop, Docs Drift Collector, Fleet Coordination Loop) · 8 Runtime starters · Maturity Model (levels 0–6, manual prompting → production-supervised) · 989-resource atlas.
- TAXONOMY.md dimensions: six loop **layers** (model / agent / harness / workflow / operations / evaluation); **trigger types** (scheduled, event-triggered, goal-driven, manual bootstrap); **work intake** (queue, scan, reactive); **verification** (deterministic, evaluator, human-supervised, receipt-based); **state models** (stateless retry, file-backed, issue-backed, checkpointed); **agent topologies** (single-agent, maker-checker, manager-worker, adversarial); **operating domains** (repository, release, feedback, evaluation).

**Mapping to your four axes:**
1. **Control-plane location** — closest match is the layer split: "harness layer" vs "workflow layer" (triggers, intake, delegation, verification, budgets, next-action policy live outside the agent). The Loop Contract is exactly an externalized, reviewable control plane. Agent topologies (manager-worker vs single-agent) also touch this. No direct "prompt-sequenced vs code/DAG-sequenced" term.
2. **Trigger model** — covered head-on and better-developed than your draft: scheduled / event-triggered / goal-driven / manual bootstrap, plus the intake split (queue / scan / reactive) which your axes don't distinguish from triggering.
3. **Isolation substrate** — their term is **workspace**: "worktree, sandbox, branch, container, read-only mode." Thinner than your axis (no local-vs-remote-fleet distinction).
4. **Autonomy scope** — the Maturity Model (0–6) plus **exit condition** and **budget**; level 2+ ("no manual launch needed") vs level 6 ("production-supervised") roughly spans bounded-task → continuous intake. "Discover/Intake" is their word for continuous intake.

**Glossary-worthy vocabulary** (beyond your draft): **loop contract**, **intake/discover** (queue/scan/reactive), **verification gate** and **maker/checker separation**, **receipt** / receipt-based verification, **durable state** (file-backed vs issue-backed vs checkpointed), **budget**, **escalation**, **exit condition**, **loop maturity level**, **goal-driven trigger**. Their "workspace" ≈ your isolation substrate; their "runtime" ("executable platform that wires a contract to a session, schedule, CI event, or durable worker") ≈ your execution layer.

**Execution runtimes/orchestrators it lists** (systems that spawn/manage agent loops, not harnesses): its own 8 runtime starters are mostly thin wrappers (Claude Code `/loop`, shell/cron loop, desktop scheduled task, Codex automation, GitHub agentic workflow). Real external systems listed: **GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw)**, **Cursor Cloud Agents/Automations**, **Google Jules**, **Cognition Devin**, **Amp orbs**, **Claude Routines/Managed Agents**, **Microsoft Agent Framework durable workflows**, **LangChain DeepAgents**, plus small orchestration tools **opencode-scheduler** (different-ai), **kanban-md** (antopolskiy). Notably it does *not* list Conductor, container-use, Sculptor, Vibe-Kanban, warren, or bernstein — its lens is recurrence/scheduling, not fleet/workspace orchestration, so it complements rather than overlaps your wiki.

## Part 2 — Ingest candidates (ranked)

1. **GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw)** — github.com/github/gh-aw, docs at github.github.com/gh-aw. Markdown+frontmatter workflows compiled to Actions lock files; agent jobs sandboxed read-only with "safe outputs" write gating. Axis position: control plane fully in code/DAG (compiled, not prompt-sequenced), event/cron-triggered, remote CI-runner isolation, continuous intake ("Continuous AI"). The only strong open example of the event-driven/in-repo-control-plane quadrant; in GitHub technical preview with heavy docs. Strongest new pick.
2. **OpenHands (+ software-agent-sdk)** — github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk, docs.openhands.dev/sdk, arXiv:2511.03690. Open-source (MIT) agent runtime with agent-server, Docker sandbox lifecycle control, remote workspaces, multi-LLM routing. Axis position: SDK/code control plane with a self-hostable remote fleet substrate — the open-source counterpart to your sandcastle+bernstein territory. Massive adoption (~50k+ stars) and a paper to ingest.
3. **Dagger container-use** — github.com/dagger/container-use. MCP server giving each agent a fresh container + git branch (Dagger + worktrees). Axis position: pure isolation-substrate play — container-per-agent local sandbox, harness-agnostic via MCP, control plane stays in the agent. Distinct because isolation is delivered *as a tool to the agent* rather than by an outer orchestrator. Already on your undocumented list; confirmed strong.
4. **Imbue Sculptor** — github.com/imbue-ai/sculptor, imbue.com/product/sculptor + several engineering blog posts (e.g. cached devcontainer images for 10x faster sandbox start). Desktop app running parallel Claude Code agents in per-agent Docker containers with Pairing Mode. Axis position: human-invoked, local container isolation (explicitly "without worktrees"), bounded tasks with tight steering — the HITL-maximal corner. Active and shipping (releases through May 2026). Confirmed strong.
5. **Conductor (Melty Labs)** — conductor.build, docs.conductor.build. Mac app: parallel Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/OpenCode agents, one git worktree per workspace, diff/PR/merge flow. Axis position: the canonical worktree-isolation, human-invoked, bounded-task orchestrator. Closed-source, but docs are substantial. Good contrast page with Sculptor (worktree vs container).
6. **Vibe-Kanban (BloopAI)** — github.com/BloopAI/vibe-kanban. Kanban board as control plane over multiple agents (parallel/sequenced), harness-agnostic. Axis distinctive: task-queue-as-control-plane, queue intake. **Caveat: Bloop shut down April 2026 and the project is sunset/community-maintained** — still worth a page (Apache-2.0 source, ~24-27k stars) but document it as historical.

**Verdict on the already-named four:** yes, three of them (container-use, Sculptor, Conductor) remain among the strongest picks and should be documented; Vibe-Kanban drops to "document as sunset." The two genuinely new strong candidates the research surfaced are **gh-aw** and **OpenHands** — both fill quadrants (event-driven CI control plane; open-source remote-fleet SDK) that none of your current pages cover. Weaker/hosted-only alternatives considered and set aside: Google Jules, Devin, Cursor Cloud Agents, Amp orbs (thin public source, product docs only); opencode-scheduler and kanban-md (too small).

Capture written to `/Users/paulmackay/dev/vaults/sdlc-wiki/raw/runtime/2026-09-01-gh-aw.md` (~300 lines, 13 source pages mirrored). Structured summary:

**1. Identity.** GitHub Agentic Workflows (`gh-aw`), a `gh` CLI extension at `github/gh-aw`. MIT license, 5,074 stars, repo created 2025-08-12, latest release v0.87.10 (2026-08-31). **Technical preview** per the GitHub blog announcement (2026-02-13, Don Syme & Peli de Halleux): "GitHub Agentic Workflows are now available in technical preview." **2. Architecture.** Workflows are Markdown + YAML frontmatter; `gh aw compile` (developer runs it locally/CI, committed alongside) produces a hardened `.lock.yml` GitHub Actions workflow — pipeline: schema validation → expression allowlisting (no secrets in expressions) → action SHA pinning → actionlint/zizmor/poutine scanners → lock file. The compiled workflow decomposes into jobs: pre-activation (role/deadline/skip checks) → activation (event-text sanitization) → **read-only agent job** (engine runs on the Actions runner, optionally inside the Agent Workflow Firewall container with Squid-proxy domain allowlist, gVisor or KVM microVM options) → isolated threat-detection job → scoped safe-output write jobs. Three-layer trust model (substrate / configuration / plan).

**3. Engines.** Five official, via `engine:`: `copilot` (default, Copilot CLI), `claude` (Claude Code, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), `codex` (OpenAI Codex), `gemini` (Gemini CLI), `pi` — all documented as production; each engine's native CLI is auto-installed. Custom engines only via nested `engine.id` referencing imports ("There is no flat `engine: custom` value"). Repo contains **unsupported samples** (OpenCode, Aider, Crush, Cursor, DeepSeek Harness, Kiro, Pydantic AI) — "samples only... not officially supported." So `runs:` edges: copilot, claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, pi.

**4. Triggers.** All GitHub Actions events (issues, PR, issue_comment, repository_dispatch, workflow_run, deployment_status, pull_request_target), cron plus fuzzy schedules ("daily around 14:00" — scattered execution), `workflow_dispatch`, `slash_command` (`/investigate`), `label_command`, plus natural-language shorthands (`on: push to main`). Trigger-level guards: `roles:` (exact-match allowlist, default admin/maintainer/write), `bots:`, `skip-if-match` search queries, `cooldown`, `stop-after: "+7d"`, `manual-approval` (environment gate).

**5. Safe outputs.** Agent job never has write permissions; it emits structured requests buffered as `agent_output.json` artifacts, a detection job vets them, then separate jobs with minimal scoped tokens apply them. ~45 typed outputs: create-issue, add-comment, create-pull-request, push-to-pull-request-branch, add-labels, create-discussion, dispatch-workflow, create-code-scanning-alert, upload-asset, etc., each with `max`, `target-repo` (multi-repo), `expires`, dedup/grouping options. Items carry a hidden `gh-aw-workflow-id` marker. Default when unspecified: create-issue with max 1.

**6. Security.** Blog verbatim: "Workflows run with read-only permissions by default. Write operations require explicit approval through safe outputs, which map to pre-approved, reviewable GitHub operations." Architecture verbatim: "The agent never requires write permissions because all write operations are performed by separate, validated jobs with minimal scoped permissions." Threat model assumes adversaries "behave arbitrarily within the privileges granted to them." Input sanitization (@mention neutralization, URI redaction, 0.5MB/65k-line truncation), integrity filtering by author trust (`merged`/`approved`/`unapproved`/`none`), unconditional secret redaction, network egress allowlist via AWF/Squid, `strict: true` default.

**7. State/memory.** `cache-memory` (Actions cache, 10GB/repo, ~7-day eviction, sanitized file types, integrity-aware keys), `repo-memory` (git branches, unlimited, versioned), private-preview `drive-memory`. Concurrency: auto per-issue/PR/ref groups plus a **global per-engine group** ("only one agent job runs per engine across all workflows"), queued not dropped. Budgets: `max-ai-credits` (default 1000/run), `max-daily-ai-credits`, `max-turns` (default 500), `user-rate-limit`, `timeout-minutes`, `stop-after`, `cooldown`.

**8. Governance/audit.** Per-run artifacts (prompt.txt, agent_output.json, aw.patch, engine + firewall logs); `gh aw logs`, `gh aw audit` (per-run reports, multi-run diff), `gh aw health` (success/cost/token trends over 7/30/90 days), `gh aw forecast` (AI-credit forecasting), `gh aw outcomes` (safe-output disposition), `gh aw models` (pricing catalog), OpenTelemetry export via `observability:`.

**9. Distinguishers vs Warren/Bernstein-style orchestrators.** The control plane is *compiled into CI*: no daemon or server — governance is enforced at compile time (lock file, SHA pinning, scanners) and by GitHub Actions job topology (write authority structurally separated into distinct jobs, not runtime policy checks). Event-driven quadrant: triggers are the repo's own event stream rather than a polling loop. Fleet management via `gh aw deploy` (org-wide rollout through PRs) and `source:`-based 3-way-merge updates.
